# The Sister App Is Bigger: Motivation, the 1,081,717-Rating Half of the Affirmation Shelf

*We run Anicca, a small daily affirmation app. For two weeks we have been measuring "I am," the biggest affirmation app on the store. This week we measured its sister app — Motivation – Daily quotes, by the same studio, Monkey Taps — which turns out to be even bigger, and we re-measured I am for the third time with the same definitions. All numbers were measured on November 26, 2026, from primary sources (the App Store listings, Apple's lookup and search APIs, the apps' review feeds, and their Instagram accounts) unless a source is explicitly marked as a third-party estimate. The series so far: [the I am teardown](https://aniccaai.com/blog/i-am-affirmation-app-deep-dive-en) and [the 7-day follow-up](https://aniccaai.com/blog/i-am-affirmation-app-followup-7-days-en).*

![Headline: Motivation deep dive, week 3](https://aniccaai.com/blog/motivation-daily-quotes-deep-dive-en/cover-motivation-deep-dive-2026-11-26.svg)

---

## TL;DR

One studio owns both halves of the shelf. Motivation holds **1,081,717 US ratings** — more than I am's 740,624 — and is adding them faster (**~168 a day** vs I am's ~144 a day this week). The two apps split App Store search between them and finish 1–2 or 1–3 on every term that matters. They run the same template — widget-first listing, ten price points, a release roughly every six days, the identical review-request line in every release note — pointed at two different vocabularies: affirmations ("I am…") and quotes. On Instagram, Motivation's account (1,675,303 followers) differs from its sister in one instructive way: **every post carries the product in a fixed caption template**, where I am mentions the app about once a week.

![Chart: new US ratings per day, 2026-11-19 to 2026-11-26 — Motivation 168, I am 144, Anicca (US) 0. n = 7 days × 3 apps. Source: Apple iTunes Lookup API, measured by Anicca.](https://aniccaai.com/blog/motivation-daily-quotes-deep-dive-en/chart-ratings-per-day-2026-11-26.svg)

![Diagram: Monkey Taps runs two apps that split the search shelf — I am takes the affirmation terms, Motivation takes the quote terms, on one shared template.](https://aniccaai.com/blog/motivation-daily-quotes-deep-dive-en/diagram-monkey-taps-shelf-2026-11-26.svg)

## Motivation, measured

**Motivation – Daily quotes** by Monkey Taps, on the store since May 13, 2014 — the same day its sister launched.

- **1,081,717 US ratings at 4.82 stars** — up **1,177 in 7 days (about 168 a day)**. Japan: 3,594 ratings. Like its sister, the engine is the US store.
- **Version 7.10.0, released November 18** — the same version number, on the same day, as I am. The studio ships both apps as one release train. Its release notes end with the exact line I am uses: *"Love the app? Tell us in the reviews section! We read all of them."*
- **Price ladder: ten in-app purchases, $3.99 to $47.99.** The ceiling is the finding: Motivation's most expensive point ($47.99) is roughly half of I am's Lifetime ($89.99). The studio prices quotes cheaper than affirmations — the same template, a different willingness to pay.
- **Subtitle unchanged: "Inspirational positive widgets."** The product is a widget that happens to contain quotes: multiple home-screen widgets, lock-screen presence, reminders through the day, 17+ quote categories, share-as-image and wallpaper export, and a blog (blog.motivation.app) linked from both the listing and every release note.
- **Premium unlocks customization, not content**: ads removed, all themes and categories, background photos, unlimited reminders, quote search. Reading and the widget stay free — the same unlock design as I am.

Here is the storefront — nine screenshots, all selling the same one thing: the first screen you see in the morning.

### The shelf, split in two

US App Store search, re-measured today for seven terms:

| Search term | Motivation | I am |
|---|---|---|
| motivation | **#1** | #2 |
| daily quotes | **#1** | #3 |
| quotes | **#1** | #2 |
| inspirational quotes | **#1** | #3 |
| daily affirmations | #2 | **#1** |
| affirmation | #3 | **#1** |
| positive affirmations | #2 | **#1** |

Neither app ever leaves the top 3. A competitor does not have to beat one winner; it has to beat the same studio twice, on two vocabularies, at once.

### Instagram: the same machine, one different gear

@motivationapp: **1,675,303 followers, 6,009 posts**. In the last 7 days it posted **28 times (4.0 a day)** — **64.3% video, 28.6% image, 7.1% carousel**, even more video-heavy than I am this week (56.7%).

The captions are where the sisters diverge. Motivation's recent image posts all use one fixed template:

> [the quote] → *"Save this for your new-year reset 🤍"* → *"I read one line like this every morning on my lock screen with the Motivation app."* → *"Comment 2027 if this is your year."*

Save CTA, keyword-comment CTA — and, in the middle, **the product itself, in every post**: the lock screen the app lives on. I am mentioned its app in 1 of 37 posts last week. Motivation mentions it in the template. The week's top posts: an image at **2,166 likes** ("Leaving this here for whoever needs it", Nov 22, [see it](https://www.instagram.com/p/DgCpfoWlv13/)) and a video at **1,910 likes** (a state-to-action prescription: "Stressed? Run. Restless? Take a nap…", Nov 22, [see it](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DgDMGAIFO6M/)).

Reviews (49 most recent, US): 31 five-star, 9 one-star. Praise centers on timing — a notification arriving when it is needed. Complaints are specific and fixable: profanity slipping into the quote pool, and a "tap to keep getting reminders" prompt users find annoying. The winner bleeds on content curation and control, not on the concept.

## I am, third measurement

Same definitions as November 12 and 19:

- **740,624 US ratings (+1,011 in 7 days, ~144 a day)** — the pace *rose* from ~118 a day last week. Japan: 1,780 (+1).
- **Still #1** on "daily affirmations", "affirmation", and "positive affirmations". No new version this week (7.10.0 of Nov 18 stands) — the six-day release cadence skipped a beat; the rating pace rose anyway.
- Instagram: **1,824,661 followers (+2,222 in 7 days, slower than last week's +3,436)**, 5,624 posts (+30). This week's 30 posts: 56.7% video, 30.0% image, 13.3% carousel. Top post: an image, **5,575 likes** — *"My peace is non-negotiable. save this for the moment you need it most."* (Nov 24, [see it](https://www.instagram.com/p/DgIH7V8Eer3/)). The save-CTA, again, is the week's maximum.

## What we learned

1. **The unit of competition is the studio, not the app.** Two mid-sized templates on two vocabularies beat one perfect app on one vocabulary, because search is the shelf and the shelf has more than one word on it.
2. **Price follows the vocabulary, not the template.** Identical mechanics, half the ceiling: quotes $47.99 max, affirmations $89.99 Lifetime. What the words *do* for the buyer sets the price, not what the app does.
3. **Product mention can be a template, not a campaign.** Motivation puts "on my lock screen with the Motivation app" in every caption and still gets the save/comment mechanics to work. The sister accounts are a natural A/B test run by the winner itself — and both arms are winning.
4. **A skipped release did not slow the review engine.** I am shipped nothing this week and its rating pace rose. The engine is the installed base plus the standing ask, not the release train alone.

## The scorecard: what we promised on November 19

| Commitment | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Fix the format, not the volume (video-first mix) | **Not done** | Our English account posted *more* — 799 → 856 posts (+57, ~8.1 a day) — but the sampled posts of Nov 25 are all images, captions are affirmation text plus hashtags. (Full-week format mix: not obtained; the connector return was truncated.) |
| Put the mechanic in the creative (date-claims, Type YES) | **Not done** | No Type-YES / save-this / screenshot-this CTA in the sampled captions; 0 likes and 0 comments on the sampled posts |
| Add the review line to release notes + rating prompt | **Not done** | **Anicca 1.11.1 shipped Nov 23** — its release notes (read today) carry no review request. In-app prompt impressions this week: not measured |
| Correct the stale lifetime price in our description | **Not done** | Our description still prints "Lifetime — $59.99" (dated Nov 6) against the store's $89.99 IAP |
| Re-measure Nov 26 + Motivation teardown | **Done** | This article |

And the rest of our week, measured: in the Nov 18–24 window we had 489 store impressions → 157 page views → **7 downloads** (Japan 5, Saudi Arabia 1, China 1; the US funnel was 218 → 5 → **0**). Japan ratings rose 48 → **49**; US ratings stayed at **1**. Our tracked keywords remain outside the top 8 for the **15th straight day**. Our Instagram followers are unchanged at **3**. Our MRR has not been re-measured since November 7 ($20) — we will not print a fresher number we do not have.

## The gap, updated

| Metric | Motivation | I am | Anicca (us) |
|---|---|---|---|
| US ratings | 1,081,717 (+1,177 this week) | 740,624 (+1,011) | **1** (+0) |
| US search rank (own terms) | #1 ×4 | #1 ×3 | Outside top 8, all tracked terms |
| Instagram followers | 1,675,303 | 1,824,661 (+2,222) | **3** (+0) |
| Posts per day (Instagram) | 4.0 | 4.3 | ~8.1 — volume copied, again |
| Video share of posts | 64.3% | 56.7% | 0% in the sampled posts |
| Top price point | $47.99 | $89.99 Lifetime | $89.99 Lifetime (description still says $59.99) |
| 7-day downloads | Not public | Not public | 7 (US: 0) |

## What we do next, in order

1. **Stop grading volume; start grading the template.** Our production brief changes from "posts per day" to the winner's caption template itself: one affirmation → a save line → one line naming the lock screen the app lives on → one keyword-comment CTA. If a post has no mechanic, it does not ship.
2. **Video share is a hard floor, not a target**: at least half of every day's posts in video form, matching the measured 57–64% band of both winners this week.
3. **Ship the two stale fixes in the next release, not a backlog**: the release-note review line, and the description's Lifetime price corrected to $89.99. Both have now been promised in print twice; a third miss gets reported as a broken process, not a delay.
4. **Re-measure again in 7 days** (December 3) with the same definitions. The next full teardown takes the #3 app on the field map: **Gratitude: Self-Care Journal** (44,994 US ratings at the last count) — the bundle winner that sells a journal, affirmations, and a vision board as one habit.

## Copy this to your agent

If you compete in a category with a dominant studio, paste this into your agent (Muse, Grok, Codex — any of them) and run the sister-app teardown exactly like this:

```text
You are my category researcher. The category winner has a sister app
from the same studio. Measure both, using only free sources, on the
same day, with the same definitions:

1. Pull both listings (lookup API + store page): version and release
   date, rating count and score, every in-app purchase price,
   subtitle, screenshot URLs. Diff the templates field by field and
   report where they are identical and where they deliberately differ
   (especially the top price point).
2. Build the search-shelf table: for every search term either app
   could own, record both apps' ranks. Report which terms each app
   owns and whether any term has neither in the top 3.
3. Pull both social profiles and every post from the last 7 days.
   Report posts/day, format mix, and — caption by caption — whether
   the product is mentioned. Quote the exact caption template if one
   repeats.
4. Read the 50 most recent reviews of the sister app. Report the star
   distribution and the specific, fixable complaints.
5. Grade EVERY commitment from our last article as done / not done /
   not measured, each with a measured number. Where our number does
   not exist, write "not measured" — never estimate our side.
6. Write it as: sister-app numbers → the shelf table → what we
   learned → the commitment scorecard → updated gap table → next
   actions in order. Include at least one chart built from the
   measured data and one diagram, each captioned with n and source.
   Mark third-party estimates as estimates and anything unobtained
   as "not obtained".
7. Save the research file, publish the article, hand the same text to
   every channel, and schedule the next re-measurement in 7 days.
```

## Our wins and losses, on the record

**Losses:** Four of last week's five commitments are simply not done — the same two cheap fixes (release-note review line, stale description price) have now been missed twice in print. Our US store funnel converted 218 impressions into 0 downloads for the second straight week. We posted ~8 times a day into 3 followers and, in the sampled posts, earned 0 likes and 0 comments, because the posts still carry no mechanic. The gap to the *second* winner is larger than the gap to the first: 1,081,717 ratings to our 1.

**Wins:** Version 1.11.1 shipped on November 23, putting the model — not a settings screen — in charge of choosing each user's words and timing, which is the one axis neither winner occupies. Downloads rose 3 → 7 week over week and Japan added a rating. And the series itself held: third week, same definitions, scorecard graded against us in public. That is the compounding this series is for: make something people want, measure the winner, publish the losses, and re-measure in 7 days.

*Sources: App Store listings for Motivation – Daily quotes, I am – Daily Affirmations, and Anicca (read Nov 26, 2026); Apple iTunes Lookup and Search APIs (Nov 26, 2026); Motivation and I am US review feeds, most recent 49 each (Nov 26, 2026); Instagram @motivationapp, @iam.affirmations, and @anicca.en profiles and posts via connector (Nov 26, 2026); our own App Store Connect aggregates (window Nov 18–24, 2026) and ASO daily ledger (OwlASO, Nov 26, 2026); prior measurements: our field map and teardowns of November 12 and 19, 2026. Revenue for I am (~$702K/month) remains an October 2026 third-party estimate (Airbridge) and was not re-measured this week; no third-party estimate for Motivation was obtained.*
